title: Sell Mineral Rights in Jansen, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Jansen, CO | Raton Basin CBM
metaDescription: Own coalbed methane minerals near Jansen, Las Animas County? We price Raton Basin interests off decline data and close directly.
heroLead: Jansen sits close to Trinidad in Las Animas County, inside the Colorado Raton Basin, where coalbed methane wells have produced from the Vermejo and Raton coal seams since the 1990s.
intro: This part of southern Colorado has a mining history that runs deeper than oil and gas, and mineral ownership near Jansen often reflects that layered past: coal rights, ranching land, and, separately, a Raton Basin coalbed methane lease that may or may not still be active.
We start by confirming exactly what your deed conveys and whether the interest has ever been leased, since those two facts determine everything about how we price it.

sections.heading: A basin with a long, slow decline
paragraphs: Coalbed methane wells in this field decline gradually compared to horizontal shale wells, which means an older Jansen-area interest can still carry real value if it is still producing. We price off your actual check stub trend rather than a generic assumption.

sections.heading: What multiple past operators tell us
paragraphs: If your Jansen-area check stubs list more than one operator name over the years, that history actually helps us, since it confirms the well has a long, real production record across ownership changes rather than a short, uncertain one. We treat that consistency as a positive input to the offer.

sections.heading: Coal history and split mineral estates
paragraphs: Given the area's coal mining past, some deeds here separate coal rights from oil and gas rights. We review your deed carefully to confirm exactly what mineral interest is on the table before making an offer.

sections.heading: Verifying through Las Animas County
paragraphs: We pull recorded leases and unit agreements from the Las Animas County Clerk and Recorder, since this basin's operator history involves several transitions over the decades that we need to reconcile against your division order.

faqs.question: Is this the same basin as the wells around Trinidad?
faqs.answer: Yes, Jansen sits within the same Raton Basin coalbed methane field that extends across this part of Las Animas County near Trinidad.

faqs.question: Does my deed include coal rights as well as oil and gas?
faqs.answer: It depends on the specific language. We check your deed to confirm exactly what you own.

faqs.question: Why has this field kept producing for so long?
faqs.answer: Coalbed methane wells decline gradually once past their early dewatering phase, supporting long production runs relative to shale wells.

faqs.question: Does having had several past operators hurt the value of my interest?
faqs.answer: No, it actually confirms a long, consistent production history across ownership changes, which we treat as a positive factor.
